cards.text: Pull up a stool, friend. The writer of this letter calls the believers he's writing to little children, and he's just warned them about people trying to deceive them (1 John 2:26). Now he tells them to remain in Christ, and he's got his eye on the day Christ appears.

cards.question: The writer tells the little children to remain in Christ. What does he want for them when Christ appears?

answers.text: To be confident and unashamed before Him
To be the very first ones He greets
To be given more than everyone else

cards.text: Then the writer reasons it out. If you know He is righteous, you also know something about everyone who practices righteousness.

cards.question: True or false: The writer says everyone who practices righteousness has been born of Him.

cards.text: Then the writer just STOPS, and I think he can't get over it: look at the love the Father has given us! Friend, I came out of a bin with a 25-cent sticker on me, so I know a LITTLE something about getting picked up when nobody had to.

cards.question: Because of the love the Father has given, what does the writer say believers are called?
True or false: The writer says being called children of God is only a title and not what believers really are.

cards.text: But heads up, friend. The writer says the world does not know us, and he says there's a reason for that.

cards.question: Why does the writer say the world doesn't know God's children?

cards.text: We're children of God right NOW, the writer says, but what we will be hasn't been revealed yet. It's me with my face pressed on the oven glass going, "Is it done? Is it DONE? What's it gonna LOOK like?" and the oven just sits there like, not yet, Papa.

cards.question: What does the writer say God's children will be when Christ appears?
The writer gives a reason believers will be like Christ when He appears. What is it?

answers.text: They will see Him as He is
They will hear His voice call them
They will sit at His table with Him

cards.text: Now THAT is a hope worth holding onto, friend! And the writer says everyone who has this hope does something about himself.

cards.question: The writer says everyone who has this hope in Christ purifies himself, just as Christ is ___.

cards.text: Now the writer turns to sin, and he does NOT tiptoe. He's been talking about practicing righteousness, and now he looks at the opposite.

cards.question: What does the writer say about everyone who practices sin?

answers.text: He has only made a mistake
He is still learning the law

cards.text: Then he puts it flat: sin is lawlessness. But he reminds them of something they already know: Christ appeared, and He came for a reason.

cards.question: The writer says Christ appeared to take away ___.
True or false: The writer says there is no sin in Christ.

cards.text: Then the writer draws a line: no one who remains in Him keeps on sinning. Now, I REMAINED in the back of a junk drawer for years, but friend, that is a VERY different kind of remaining.

cards.question: What does the writer say about someone who continues to sin?

answers.text: He has not seen or known Christ
He is closer to Christ than he thinks
He only needs one more warning

cards.text: The writer's calling them little children again, and he's got a warning: don't let anyone deceive you. And what he wants them clear on is who's righteous.

cards.question: True or false: The writer warns the little children that whoever claims to be righteous is righteous, no matter how he lives.

cards.text: Then the writer goes all the way back. The one who practices sin is of the devil, he says, because the devil has been sinning from the very start.

cards.question: True or false: The writer says the Son of God was revealed to destroy the works of the devil.

cards.text: Then the writer says anyone born of God refuses to practice sin. He goes even further: that person cannot go on sinning, because he has been born of God.

cards.question: The writer gives another reason someone born of God refuses to practice sin. What is it?

answers.text: The fear of judgment holds him back
His temptations have all gone away

cards.text: So how do you tell the children of God from the children of the devil? The writer says anyone who does not practice righteousness is not of God.

cards.question: The writer gives one more sign that someone is not of God. What is it?

answers.text: He does not love his brother
He does not know the law
He does not keep the feasts
